alternates.speaker: Rama

alternates.line: Teach me how to keep working in the world without the work filling me with sorrow.

prasang.story_hook: Having said what was wrong, Rama finally asked the question that matters: how do the wise do it?
prasang.lesson: The real question isn't whether to quit life, but how to live it without being swallowed.

alternates.speaker: Tulsidas
alternates.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram, slowed by shame, quickened by love.
alternates.sanskrit: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
alternates.line: Shame slowed him. But whenever he remembered Ram's nature, his feet moved faster.
alternates.translation: It was as if his mother's wrong held him back, while the strength of devotion drove him on like a patient ox. Whenever he remembered Raghunath's nature, his feet moved faster on the path.

verse.speaker: Janaka
verse.setting: Janaka, having chosen to keep ruling, talks gently to his own restless mind at night.
verse.sanskrit: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥
verse.line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
verse.translation: The more you casually spin up fancies and possibilities, the more your world of troubles swells, through your own worrying.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.for_you: Yesterday's verse spoke of the rain of calm. Today, Janaka asks why your mind spins so many scenarios, and how that feeds the worry that keeps you up at 3am.
verse.try_today: Notice one thought you spin up today that grows the world of worry.
verse.scene_line: You run between the hospital and the office, and your mind spins survival rates at 3am.

why: Worry grows when you feed it (Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6)
the swelling is traced to the spinning, which can be stopped

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on worship for rewards and worship without desire.
verse.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
verse.line: Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.
verse.translation: To those who think of me alone and worship me, ever devoted, I bring what they lack and preserve what they have.
verse.why: Trust eases the worry of getting and keeping.
verse.misuse: Not 'God will pay the bills, so don't plan'. Trust eases worry; it doesn't replace effort or prudence.

prasang.title: Worship with and without desire, and their fruits
prasang.summary: Those who worship for heavenly rewards return when merit runs out; those who think of him alone are carried and protected.
prasang.lesson: Trust eases the worry of getting and keeping.

verse.for_you: Yesterday the Yoga Vasishtha showed how your mind spins scenarios. Today, you can set down the weight of keeping everything, and let the one who guards what you have hold the hospital, the office, and the night.
verse.try_today: At 3am, let the search end and the guarding begin.

why: The child relies on the mother and stops worrying.
the worry of getting and keeping is carried by God for the one wholly turned to him

verse.setting: Karma-Yoga classes, New York, 1895–96, chapter 7, on 'slaves to duty'.
verse.line: Be at rest, be free, and work.
verse.translation: Duty becomes a disease with us; it drags us ever forward. … They come home and think of the work for the next day. … Be at rest, be free, and work.
verse.why: Be at rest, be free, and work.
verse.misuse: Not permission to drop real responsibilities; it is about working without compulsion.

prasang.title: Karma-Yoga 7: freedom
prasang.summary: Misery comes from attachment, not work. He attacks duty that has become a compulsion and asks for work done freely. The greatest people often die unknown, so seek no praise.
prasang.lesson: Be at rest, be free, and work.

verse.for_you: Today you can see that duty has become a disease. Be at rest, be free, and work.
verse.try_today: Notice when duty pulls you forward, and pause to rest before you move.
verse.scene_line: You run between the hospital, the office, and home, yet the work for tomorrow still waits.

verse.speaker: The gods
verse.setting: Part of the closing hymn to the Goddess.
verse.sanskrit: नमामि त्वामहं देवीं महाभयविनाशिनीम् । महादुर्गप्रशमनीं महाकारुण्यरूपिणीम् ॥
verse.line: I bow to you, Goddess: you end great fear, you ease great hardship, you are compassion itself.
verse.translation: I bow to you, Goddess, destroyer of great fear, who calms great hardship, whose very form is great compassion.
verse.why: The Mother who is everything is also near enough to be called on in fear.
verse.misuse: Praise of the Goddess's compassion, not a promise that hardship will disappear; seek practical help too.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्
verse.line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
verse.translation: A leader should never show fear in any crisis. Even if shaken inside, he should not act like a shaken man.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.misuse: This is about not acting from panic, not about hiding your feelings from everyone.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

why: Bearing of fearlessness
Courage and steadiness are the wheels of the chariot that wins; do not let fear decide.
plan_v3.writer_note: The person mentioned medication, detox or treatment. This verse is about resolve or not stopping: apply it only to the other parts of their life they named, never to their medication or treatment. Never imply a medical decision, a pace or a deadline for one.

story.title: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
story.story_hook: High on a mountain lived a crow who had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall.
story.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow arrogant from knowing, and shares in others' joys and sorrows.
story.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.
story.hook_title: An old crow had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall, untroubled
story.teaser: An old crow had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall, untroubled
story.for_you: Yesterday’s verse said fear should not steer your choices. Bhushunda shows the next step: a steady gaze at the breath keeps the past and future from burning you. Your mind may keep circling, but you can rest here now.

plan_v3.path: st.yv.bhushunda_the_old_crow -enacts_in-> bhaya, chinta ; st.yv.bhushunda_the_old_crow -enacts_turn-> abhaya, shanti ; st.yv.bhushunda_the_old_crow -fits_situation-> fear_death
why: Death and fear find little hold on the one who watches the breath and is not burned by worries about past and future.

verse.speaker: Bhasa
verse.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
verse.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
verse.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
verse.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
verse.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

verse.for_you: You are moving between the hospital, the office, and home alone, and at three in the morning your mind still searches for answers. The weight of all these tasks is heavy, and the mind gets no moment’s rest. You can let the lists be for now.
verse.try_today: Notice one task you are doing, and let the mind rest from the next one.

why: its depths dance with worry
caught in a net of done, doing, to do

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥
verse.line: When the mind chases a wandering sense, it is swept off like a boat in the wind.
verse.translation: When the mind runs after the roving senses, it carries away one's understanding, as the wind carries a boat away on the water.
verse.why: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

prasang.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

verse.for_you: Yesterday your mind found no rest in lists. Now it is swept away by the wind of every worry. The mind that follows the senses carries off your understanding.
verse.try_today: Notice where your mind goes when it leaves the room.

why: The boat and the wind (Bhagavad Gita 2.60)
shows the mechanism: the mind follows one sense and the whole understanding is blown off course

verse.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verse.setting: Uddalaka explains sleep to his son.
verse.sanskrit: स यथा शकुनिः सूत्रेण प्रबद्धो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनमलब्ध्वा बन्धनमेवोपश्रयत एवमेव खलु सोम्य तन्मनो दिशं दिशं पतित्वान्यत्रायतनमलब्ध्वा प्राणमेवोपश्रयते प्राणबन्धनꣳ हि सोम्य मन इति ॥
verse.line: Like a bird on a string, the mind flies everywhere, finds no rest, and returns to the breath.
verse.translation: As a bird tied by a string flies in every direction and, finding no resting place anywhere else, settles down at the very place it is tied, so, dear one, the mind flies in every direction and, finding no resting place anywhere else, settles down on the breath; for the mind is tied to the breath.
verse.why: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

prasang.title: Uddalaka's lessons: tat tvam asi
prasang.summary: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'
prasang.lesson: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

verse.for_you: Now it has a string and a place to land. You run between three places and the mind runs with you. It will find its way back to the life you are tied to.
verse.try_today: Notice where your mind returns when it stops flying.

why: the flying about ends in rest, every night
the restless mind is not broken; it has a home it returns to

verse.line: An arrow-maker was so absorbed in his work, he didn't notice the king walking past.
verse.translation: A certain arrow-maker was so absorbed in his arrow that he did not even notice the king passing right beside him.
verse.why: Learn from everything. Drop what makes you a target, and give your work full attention.

prasang.title: Bodhya's teachers
prasang.summary: Asked how he found peace, the sage Bodhya names his teachers: Pingala, the osprey that dropped its scrap of meat and was left alone, the snake, the deer, the arrow-maker so absorbed he did not see the king pass, and a girl's bangle.
prasang.lesson: Learn from everything. Drop what makes you a target, and give your work full attention.

verse.try_today: Notice one small task you do today with complete attention, and let everything else go.
verse.scene_line: You are the arrow-maker, and the king of your worry passes by unnoticed.

why: Absorption as rest from distraction
Single-pointed attention to the work in hand

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

verse.for_you: An arrow-maker lost in his work did not notice the king. Your mind is busy with survival rates and hospital halls. Rest in what is happening now.
verse.try_today: Notice one unplanned pleasure that comes to you today.
verse.scene_line: You sit at 3am with your mother's treatment and your own fear.

why: Vishramyatam
Enjoying what arrives unplanned

story.title: Kabir to his own restless mind: slowly, slowly
story.story_hook: The gardener can pour a hundred pots of water. The mango still waits for its season.
story.summary: The mind wants the result now. Kabir talks to it the way a gardener would.
story.lesson: Water faithfully; the fruit comes in its season, not because you poured more.
story.teaser: The gardener can pour a hundred pots of water. The mango still waits for its season.
story.for_you: Yesterday we rested the mind from replaying the past or scripting the future. Today, Kabir asks you to keep watering while the fruit comes in its own time.

verse.speaker: Yudhishthira
verse.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verse.sanskrit: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा / मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्
verse.line: The mind is faster than the wind, and worries outnumber the blades of grass.
verse.translation: Yaksha: 'What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than blades of grass?' Yudhishthira: 'A mother is heavier than the earth; a father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; worries are more numerous than blades of grass.'
verse.why: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

prasang.title: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.story_hook: Four brothers lay dead by a clear lake, and the voice that killed them was asking Yudhishthira riddles.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

verse.for_you: Your mind is running between the hospital, the office and the dark hours of the night. The worries are more numerous than blades of grass, and the mind is faster than the wind. The weight of your mother and father is heavier than the earth, and higher than the sky.
verse.try_today: Notice one worry, and let it be only a worry.
verse.scene_line: You sit at 3am with the weight of the world, and the mind outruns the wind.

why: Worries counted as more than blades of grass
The mind outruns the wind

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse.sanskrit: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥
verse.line: Even a wise, striving person can be dragged off by restless senses. Don't be surprised; be ready.
verse.translation: The turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise person who is striving, Arjuna.
verse.why: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

prasang.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

verse.for_you: Even a wise, striving person can have the mind carried off by restless senses. You are trying to hold everything together, and the pull is stronger than you expect.
verse.try_today: Notice when your mind is pulled away from the present moment.

why: The boat and the wind (Bhagavad Gita 2.60)
the pull of the senses is named as strong, so a slip is no surprise

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: The famous verse closing the Brahmananda Valli.
verse.sanskrit: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह । आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान्। न बिभेति कुतश्चनेति ।
verse.line: Where words and thoughts turn back unable to reach: whoever knows that joy fears nothing.
verse.translation: That from which words turn back, along with the mind, not reaching it: whoever knows the joy of Brahman fears nothing at all.
verse.why: The deepest joy can't be bought, and it frees you from fear and regret.

prasang.title: The measure of joy
prasang.summary: The Upanishad tries to measure joy: a young, good, strong man owning the whole earth has one unit of human joy, and each higher joy is a hundred times greater, yet each is already held by one free of desire. It ends with the joy before which words turn back, which frees a person from fear and from self-torment over past deeds.
prasang.lesson: The deepest joy can't be bought, and it frees you from fear and regret.

verse.try_today: Notice the moment your mind turns back from a worry, and let it be.
verse.scene_line: Between the hospital and the office, you stand where words turn back unable to reach.

why: the mind is told there is a place it need not, and cannot, work out
The Upanishads' root answer.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verse.sanskrit: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verse.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
verse.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.try_today: Notice one moment of outward action today and let your inside stay calm.
verse.scene_line: You run between the hospital and the office, a doer on the outside, while the world moves around you.

why: effort outside, stillness inside

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Raja-Yoga (1896), chapter 6: the first practice for a racing mind.
verse.line: Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch.
verse.translation: The first lesson, then, is to sit for some time and let the mind run on. The mind is bubbling up all the time. It is like that monkey jumping about. Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch. … But you will find that each day the mind's vagaries are becoming less and less violent, that each day it is becoming calmer.
verse.why: Watch the mind before trying to control it; calm comes with daily practice.

prasang.title: The drunken monkey: taming a restless mind
prasang.summary: The mind is a monkey made drunk by desire, stung by jealousy and possessed by pride. The first practice is to sit and watch it without fighting; each day it grows calmer. Then take up one idea and let it fill your life.
prasang.story_hook: There was a monkey, restless as all monkeys are; someone gave it wine, then a scorpion stung it, and then a demon got into it.
prasang.lesson: Watch the mind before trying to control it; calm comes with daily practice.

verse.for_you: Today, sit and let the mind run while you wait and watch. Each day it grows calmer.
verse.try_today: Notice the mind jumping and wait without fighting it.

why: calm arrives by itself, day by day
a sitting practice to repeat

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha's closing advice to Rama on living in the world after the three vows.
verse.sanskrit: अन्तर्मुखः सन्सततं समस्तं कुर्वन्बहिष्ठं खलु कार्यजातम् । न खेदमायासि कदाचिदेव निराकृताहंकृतितामुपैषि ॥
verse.line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
verse.translation: Staying turned inward while doing all the outer work that comes to you, you will never grow weary, and you will be free of the sense of being the doer.
verse.why: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

prasang.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
prasang.summary: Vasishtha gives Rama three vows that Shiva once gave his devotee Bhringi: be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer. A great doer acts fully and on time without clinging; a great enjoyer takes in joys and sorrows evenly, like the ocean takes in rivers; a great renouncer lets go inside. Live this way and work won't wear you out.
prasang.lesson: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

verse.try_today: Notice the sense of being the doer while running between the hospital, the office and home.
verse.scene_line: Vasishtha speaks to Rama about acting fully without clinging, as you move between care and work.

why: an inner anchor during activity

story.title: Ram stands exhausted and anxious before the final battle
story.story_hook: Before the last fight, even Ram stood there exhausted and worried. Then a sage came up to him.
story.summary: After days of war, Ram is worn out. Ravana is in front of him, ready for the final fight. Ram stands there sunk in thought, weighed down with worry.
story.lesson: Before the hardest moment, draw strength from what is greater than you, then act.
story.teaser: Before the last fight, even Ram stood there exhausted and worried. Then a sage came up to him.
story.for_you: Yesterday, staying anchored within helped with your exhaustion. Today, Ram shows that before the hardest moment, strength comes from something greater than you, and then you act. In your running between hospital, office, and home, you can turn to that greater strength before the next demand hits, and then move.
